messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Let's add a new feature—bots. Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

Any chat member can create and manage bots via the user interface:
- open the account settings page (`/account/edit`)
- click the bot icon ("Set up chat bots")

This opens the bots page (`/bots`). It lists the bots you created (administrators see all bots) and has the "Add a chat bot" button. The button opens the `/bots/new` page with a form:

- bot avatar (optional)
- bot name (required), labelled "Name the bot"
- the "Save changes" button

Submitting the form creates a bot and redirects back to `/bots`. Each bot on the list shows its name and its unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", in the same list item—the code is used to authenticate bot requests. The bot code is a sensitive credential. The bots page shows all of your bots on one page, without pagination.

From the list, you can also edit a bot (name, avatar): each bot has an "Edit <bot name>" link (for example, "Edit Deploy Bot") to its edit page. The edit page uses the same form and has a "Delete this chat bot" button that asks for confirmation. A deleted bot can no longer post messages.

Like any new user, a new bot joins all open rooms. Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people.

Here is how a bot can post a message:

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Bots can post from shell scripts and CI jobs. The raw request body becomes the message body. No JSON envelope, no field names.

The endpoint responds with:

- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` — empty body and no attachment
- `404 Not Found` — bad room id
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid bot code

The message is broadcast to connected clients and triggers push notifications exactly as a human-authored message would.

The message shows the bot (its name) as the author.

**Initial Assessment: Campfire - Quick Scan & Deep Dive**

Alright, a new project! My first thought is always a quick sanity check: *Do the existing tests run without immediately crashing? That's a great start.* From there, I need to understand the development environment and conventions. Let's see... I'm going to quickly scan for tell-tale signs of a well-maintained project. I'll look for things like system tests, RuboCop and Brakeman integrations - a good linting/security setup is always a plus.

Once I've got a baseline understanding, I’m immediately going to dive into the core of the application. I need to understand the data model and the routing. The *schema.rb* file is a great place to begin, followed by the *config/routes.rb* file. Then, I’ll zero in on some key model files to get a feel for how things are structured. The `User` model, specifically how it's defined and how it's used is a good starting point, and I'll extend to the other models that are related. I'll check on the architecture using `Message`, and `Room` as a further reference. My goal is to grasp the foundational architecture and the project's adherence to its conventions. This initial deep dive will give me the context I need to tackle anything that comes my way.

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception
  end

  class_methods do
    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
    end

    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end
end

      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Closed)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: converting one would let its creator revise who's in it.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def grantees
      User.where(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def revokees
      @room.users.where.not(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def grantee_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      each_user_and_html_for(room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_prepend_to user, :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, html: html
      end
    end

    def broadcast_update_room
      each_user_and_html_for(@room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_replace_to user, :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], html: html
      end
    end

    def each_user_and_html_for(room)
      # Optimization to avoid rendering the same partial for every user
      html = render_to_string(partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room })

      room.users.each { |user| yield user, html }
    end
end

    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  end

    end

## Development

### Setting up

First, get everything installed and configured with:

```sh
bin/setup
```

This installs the system packages Campfire needs (SQLite, ffmpeg), the right Ruby version (via [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev)), and the app's gems; prepares the database; and starts Redis (in a Docker container called `campfire-redis`, if it isn't already running locally).

If you want to start over at any point, run:

```sh
bin/setup --reset
```

### Running the server

Start the development server with:

```sh
bin/dev
```

You'll be able to access the app at http://localhost:3000.

On first run you'll be guided through creating your admin account, and you can sign in with that account from then on.

Note that Campfire needs Redis (for Action Cable, caching, and background jobs), so if you've restarted your machine or stopped the container, `docker start campfire-redis` will bring it back.

### Web Push notifications

Campfire uses VAPID (Voluntary Application Server Identification) keys to send browser push notifications. For notifications to work in development you'll need to generate a key pair and set these environment variables:

- `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`

You can generate a fresh pair (along with a secret key base, which you can ignore in development) by running:

```sh
script/admin/generate-secrets
```

### Running tests

Run the unit tests with:

```sh
bin/rails test
```

And the browser-based system tests with:

```sh
bin/rails test:system
```

Before pushing your changes, you can run the full CI suite locally - style checks, security audits, and all the tests - with a single command:

```sh
bin/ci
```

### Contributing

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
If you'd like to contribute your changes back, please read our [contributing guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md) first.

ENV["RAILS_ENV"] ||= "test"
require_relative "../config/environment"

require "rails/test_help"
require "mocha/minitest"
require "webmock/minitest"
require "turbo/broadcastable/test_helper"

WebMock.enable!

class ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  parallelize(workers: :number_of_processors)

  # Setup all fixtures in test/fixtures/*.yml for all tests in alphabetical order.
  fixtures :all

  include SessionTestHelper, MentionTestHelper, TurboTestHelper, NetworkTestHelper

  setup do
    ActionCable.server.pubsub.clear

    Rails.configuration.tap do |config|
      config.x.web_push_pool.shutdown
      config.x.web_push_pool = WebPush::Pool.new \
        invalid_subscription_handler: config.x.web_push_pool.invalid_subscription_handler
    end

    WebMock.disable_net_connect!
  end

  teardown do
    WebMock.reset!
  end
end

class UserTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase

    users(:david).update(password: "secret" * 50)
    assert users(:david).valid?
  end

    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      create_new_user
    end
  end

  end

    assert_response :success
    ensure_messages_present @messages.first, @messages.second
    ensure_messages_not_present @messages.third, @messages.fourth, @messages.fifth
  end

  test "index returns a page after the specified message" do
    get room_messages_url(@room, after: @messages.third)

    assert_response :success
    ensure_messages_present @messages.fourth, @messages.fifth
    ensure_messages_not_present @messages.first, @messages.second, @messages.third
  end

  test "index returns no_content when there are no messages" do
    @room.messages.destroy_all

    get room_messages_url(@room)

    assert_response :no_content
  end

  test "get renders a single message belonging to the user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:david)).first

    get room_message_url(@room, message)

    assert_response :success
  end

  test "creating a message broadcasts the message to the room" do
    post room_messages_url(@room, format: :turbo_stream), params: { message: { body: "New one", client_message_id: 999 } }

    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @room, :messages ] do
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /New one/
      assert_copy_link_button room_at_message_url(@room, Message.last, host: "once.campfire.test")
    end
  end

  test "creating a message broadcasts unread room to each member" do
    @room.users.each do |member|
      assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(member.id), 1 do
        post room_messages_url(@room, format: :turbo_stream), params: { message: { body: "New one #{member.id}", client_message_id: member.id } }
      end
    end
  end

  test "creating a message doesn't broadcast unread room to non-members" do
    outsiders = User.where.not(id: @room.users.map(&:id))
    assert outsiders.any?, "need someone outside the room for this test to mean anything"

    outsiders.each do |outsider|
      assert_no_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(outsider.id) do
        post room_messages_url(@room, format: :turbo_stream), params: { message: { body: "New one", client_message_id: 999 } }
      end
    end
  end

  test "update updates a message belonging to the user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:david)).first

    Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_replace_to).once
    put room_message_url(@room, message), params: { message: { body: "Updated body" } }

    assert_redirected_to room_message_url(@room, message)
    assert_equal "Updated body", message.reload.plain_text_body
  end

  test "admin updates a message belonging to another user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:jason)).first

    Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_replace_to).once
    put room_message_url(@room, message), params: { message: { body: "Updated body" } }

    assert_redirected_to room_message_url(@room, message)
    assert_equal "Updated body", message.reload.plain_text_body
  end

  test "destroy destroys a message belonging to the user" do

    assert_difference -> { Message.count }, -1 do
      Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_remove_to).once
      delete room_message_url(@room, message, format: :turbo_stream)
      assert_response :success
    end
  end

  test "admin destroy destroys a message belonging to another user" do
    assert users(:david).administrator?

    assert_difference -> { Message.count }, -1 do
      Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_remove_to).once
      delete room_message_url(@room, message, format: :turbo_stream)
      assert_response :success
    end
  end

  test "ensure non-admin can't update a message belonging to another user" do
    sign_in :jz
    assert_not users(:jz).administrator?

**Okay, Deep Breath! Let's Break This Down**

Right, so no chromedriver, we're rocking rack_test and full integration tests – perfect. We've got the tools to ensure everything is spot-on. Now, let's dive into this bot feature. The goal is to carefully dissect the prompt, translate the requirements into code, and adhere to Campfire conventions. It looks like the system is well set up to use existing User models.

My initial thought is that bots *should* be represented as users, likely with a designated role (possibly `:bot`). This approach leverages existing infrastructure for rooms, memberships, message creation, push notifications, and avatars. The prompt clearly states they behave like users in many respects, which is a major signal. The fact that the existing schema has `creator_id` and the original Campfire project had a similar design also points in this direction.

Let's carefully examine the prompt and the codebase to make an informed decision:

1.  Bots are members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.
2.  Like any new user, bots join all open rooms, can be added to other rooms, and are treated similarly to people.
3.  Messages are broadcast, triggering push notifications, and displaying the bot's name as the author.
4.  Bots will be created and managed via the user interface by any chat member.
5.  Administrators will see all bots.
6.  Deleted bots can no longer post messages.

Looking at the database schema, the `memberships` table's `user_id` column isn't polymorphic, and `messages` uses `creator_id`, which references the `users` table. `Users` already has the `name`, `role`, and `status` fields, and the `User::Role` enum suggests a place to store our bot roles. `User` already includes concerns like `Avatar`, `Bannable`, and `Mentionable` and `Transferable`. Bots will automatically be added to new open rooms via `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, automatically show up in member selection for direct and closed rooms, and work with the existing `Message` structure including broadcasting and push notifications.

Critically, the old Campfire project's design also had bots as users. Now, that's incredibly helpful. It's time to check what kind of additional data we would need to add to the `User` model, such as the bot code.

The next step is to carefully check the table and migration schema, and all the available details from the codebase.

**Bot Posting API Deep Dive**

Okay, here's what I'm thinking about the bot posting API. It needs to be rock solid, secure, and intuitive for both developers and users. I'm seeing a lot of consistency in Campfire's approach, which is fantastic.

First things first, the `/bots` page: the design is excellent, the visual cues for the "Add a chat bot" button are spot on, and the overall layout is clean. The focus here is on visibility and ease of use, which is critical.

Now, that crucial "Bot code." We need to treat this as the super-sensitive credential it is. The UI for the code display is nearly perfect! The key is to ensure it’s clearly labeled, and easily copyable *but* not editable. The ideal implementation should definitely be a read-only input field coupled with a "copy to clipboard" button.  Critically, the bot code itself MUST be only the bot key. No URLs, just the secret. That is *imperative*.

Now, the security implications. I'm going through the list and double-checking everything. The bot code *must* be cryptographically strong, and it seems Campfire is already on the right track with `SecureRandom`. The token should have high entropy, be URL-safe to avoid any encoding issues, and definitely *not* be predictable or sequential. I'm thinking about the difference between a bot token that has the bot's ID in it, versus a truly opaque key. An opaque key is better because it doesn't leak any identifying information. I'm also thinking about timing attacks, if the check isn't constant.

And I'm remembering this is sensitive. The application is already handling filtering, which is great. It means `bot_key` and other sensitive parameters will automatically be filtered out of controller logs! Good. Visibility is a big one; the bots' codes are only on the `/bots` page and are not exposed elsewhere. We need to be especially careful about who can *see* these codes. Regular members, administrators, and the like all have different access. We should also look into setting `Cache-Control: no-store` to prevent caching of the bot's code. And `autocomplete="off"` is good hygiene on that input.

Now, a very critical question is deleting a bot versus deactivating. If we *destroy* the bot, we also wipe out all of its messages, and that's usually bad, especially for things like automated deploys or logs. That could destroy chat history. *Deactivating* the bot is the right answer. We can handle it like a human user's deactivation. We nullify the token and mark the account as deactivated, so the bot can no longer post messages. However, its historical messages stay intact. And it's also important to make sure we clean up the bot's memberships in open or closed rooms to prevent any kind of access that it shouldn't have.

Now, let's drill down into the posting API (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`). I'm going through this line by line.

*   **The Route:** The best way to implement it is to nest the route under the existing `rooms` resource, which is fine and avoids any conflicts. That feels clean, secure, and logical.
*   **Authentication & Permissions:** The `ApplicationController` includes several critical concerns: `AllowBrowser`, `Authentication`, `Authorization`, `BlockBannedRequests`, and `SetCurrentRequest`. Since our code does not run in a browser, we are skipping the browser check. But all the other things like `require_authentication`, `protect_from_forgery`, and `SetCurrentRequest` are all important. We also need to remember to *skip* CSRF protection since this is an API. And `ActiveStorage::SetCurrent` and `SetCurrentRequest` ensure that URLs broadcast inside the streams are correct, which is essential for attachments and images. `BlockBannedRequests` adds a good measure of security. Most importantly, `@bot` is set as `Current.user` which is used to attribute a message to the bot.
*   **Status Codes:** I've carefully thought through every possible scenario. Authentication is the primary check, it is the first guard. An invalid bot code must return a `401 Unauthorized` before anything else. A good room ID or membership check before anything.  Then, a non-existent or invalid `room_id` gets a `404 Not Found`. Also, a check is needed to ensure the bot is actually *in* the specified room (also a `404 Not Found`). Now, digging into `ApplicationController._process_action_callbacks` is where things get interesting. I see `verify_authenticity_token` skipped via `skip_forgery_protection`, which makes sense. Then, there's `verify_same_origin_request`. Hang on... `skip_forgery_protection` *also* skips `verify_authenticity_token`! So, is `verify_same_origin_request` running on `POST` requests? It seems like it's only triggered for cross-origin `XHR`/`fetch` requests that are specifically in JS format, as a measure against CSRF JSONP/JS issues. It appears to skip the function call for `curl` or regular requests, as expected. Then there's `allow_browser`. Rails 8.1 uses a lambda here! I need to understand what this callback does when different `User-Agent` headers are sent, specifically with `curl/8.5.0`, `Firefox/114.0`, or no `User-Agent` at all. I also need to check how the behavior changes if `Messages::ByBotsController` inherits from `ApplicationController` versus `ActionController::Base` (or if it includes only the required concerns, or uses `allow_browser versions: ...`). And can `allow_browser` actually be overridden in a subclass? Let's check that too! Finally, let's look at how the application renders text and potential vulnerabilities. require "test_helper"

class Room::PushTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  test "deliver new message to other room users with push subscriptions" do
    task_count = Push::Subscription.count - users(:david).push_subscriptions.count
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(task_count)
      rooms(:hq).messages.create! body: "This is from earth", client_message_id: "earth", creator: users(:david)
    end
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(task_count)
  end

  test "notifies subscribed users" do
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(2)
      rooms(:designers).messages.create! body: "This is from earth", client_message_id: "earth", creator: users(:david)
    end
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(2)

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(3)
      rooms(:designers).messages.create! body: "Hey #{mention_attachment_for(:kevin)}", client_message_id: "earth", creator: users(:david)
    end
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(5)
  end

  test "does not notify for connected rooms" do
    memberships(:kevin_designers).connected

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(2)
      rooms(:designers).messages.create! body: "Hey @kevin", client_message_id: "earth", creator: users(:david)
    end
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(2)
  end

  test "does not notify for invisible rooms" do
    memberships(:kevin_designers).update! involvement: "invisible"

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(2)
      rooms(:designers).messages.create! body: "Hey @kevin", client_message_id: "earth", creator: users(:david)
    end
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(2)
  end

  test "destroys invalid subscriptions" do
    memberships(:kevin_designers).update! involvement: "invisible"

    assert_difference -> { Push::Subscription.count }, -2 do
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
        WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(2).raises(WebPush::ExpiredSubscription.new(Struct.new(:body).new, "example.com"))
        rooms(:designers).messages.create! body: "Hey @kevin", client_message_id: "earth", creator: users(:david)
      end
      wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(2)
      wait_for_invalidation_pool_tasks(2)
    end
  end

  private
    def wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(count)
      wait_for_pool_tasks(Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.delivery_pool, count)
    end

    def wait_for_invalidation_pool_tasks(count)
      wait_for_pool_tasks(Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.invalidation_pool, count)
    end

      start = Time.now
      timeout = 0.2
      while pool.completed_task_count < count
        raise "Timeout waiting for pool tasks to complete" if Time.now - start > timeout
        sleep timeout / 10.0
      end
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing the Message Creation Process**

Okay, let's break this down. First, I'm taking a look at `app/models/message.rb`. It's a fairly standard ActiveRecord model, including several modules: `Attachment`, `Broadcasts`, `Mentionee`, `Pagination`, and `Searchable`. It's got the usual associations with `room` and `creator` (a `User`, defaulting to `Current.user`), and a `has_many :boosts` association. The use of `has_rich_text :body` suggests a rich text editor is in use which is a great pattern.

The `before_create` callback is interesting; it's generating a `client_message_id` using `Random.uuid` if one doesn't already exist. That's good for unique identification. Then, after the message is created and committed to the database (in an `after_create_commit` block), a few things happen: the `room.receive(self)` method is called. This triggers several things:
*   `unread_memberships(message)` marks disconnected, visible memberships (except for the bot) as unread.
*   `push_later(message)` enqueues a `Room::PushMessageJob` which delivers web push notifications.
*   `Message::Searchable` calls `after_create_commit :create_in_index` which indexes the message into the FTS5 `message_search_index`. Very efficient for search!
*   Finally, `@message.broadcast_create` broadcasts the rendered message via Turbo Streams and `{roomId: room.id}` to every room member's `UnreadRoomsChannel` stream!

Now, hang on... let's dig into that `broadcast_unread_room` method. It looks like it iterates through the room's members and broadcasts a `roomId` to each user's `UnreadRoomsChannel` using ActionCable, which works quite seamlessly with the `Room#unread_memberships` method, which is marking the message as unread. This seems like a clever approach to updating unread counts. The `where.not(user: message.creator)` clause is exactly what I'd expect; bots don't need to mark their own messages as unread!

One last thing, I'm curious how `Messages::ByBotsController` works, specifically, let's check `config/routes.rb` for how `messages` are routed and what a `GET /messages/:message_id` does. A quick `bin/rails routes | grep messages` should help. This will show how the system routes the message boosts.

*   `update`: failure `@bot.update(bot_params)` (e.g., blank name), render `:edit, status: :unprocessable_content`.
*   And the HTML form has `<input ... required="required" ...>` for browser-side validation.

Also, it's good to check that adding `validates :name, presence: true` on `User` *won't* break any existing tests. Now, let's carefully check bot deactivation via `User#deactivate`.

In `User#deactivate`:
*   `close_remote_connections` is a harmless no-op for bots.
*   `memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all` removes the bot from all open and closed rooms.

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Message Creation and Browser Handling** Okay, first things first, let's dive into this `allow_browser.rb` code. It looks like `curl` and non-browsers are already permitted, which is great. If we ever want to bypass or customize the browser check in the future, we can add a `skip_browser_check` flag or simply inherit from `ApplicationController`. It's pretty straightforward. Thinking about `AllowBrowser` concern, if we want to change or override it in `Messages::ByBotsController`, we can simply redefine the `allow_browser` instance method. No changes in `AllowBrowser` are needed unless we want to allow *any* user-agent in `Messages::ByBotsController`. Overriding `def allow_browser(**); end` or adding `allow_any_browser` would do the trick. It seems `curl`, `Ruby`, `Python`, `Node`, `fetch`, and modern browsers already pass `allow_browser`. Perfect! Now, onto the meatier stuff – different content types in message requests: Let's dissect all of these request body scenarios very carefully. 1. `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`: When we send `curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅"`, the raw request body becomes the message body as-is. 2. Also `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`: Even complex data with `&` and `=` gets treated literally as the message body, without parsing. 3. `text/plain`: "Hello world" becomes "Hello world" with no fuss. 4. `application/json`: Raw JSON string becomes the message body. No fancy JSON parsing, which is good. 5. `multipart/form-data`: Here, we're creating with an attachment. `curl -F "attachment=@/path/to/image.png"` results in a message *with* an attachment, created with the method `@room.messages.create_with_attachment!`. In Campfire (and maybe here), a message is *either* an attachment *or* text. No mixing. If we send multipart data *without* an attachment, or with a string for attachment, we get a 422 error. Important note: Rails `fixture_file_upload` sends a `multipart/form-data` request, and Rack parses it into an `ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile`. Need to verify this in an integration test just to be 100% sure. 6. No body at all (empty POST): 422 Unprocessable Content. 7. Whitespace-only body: 422 Unprocessable Content, as expected. **Wait! What about HTML in the message body?!** Hold on a second! What if a bot sends something like ``?! This could be a security vulnerability! I need to test this. Earlier, we saw the `bin/rails runner` showing: `INPUT: ""` `plain: ""` `rendered: "
\n \n
\n"` So if someone sends `curl -d "Deploy finished"`, then it renders `Deploy finished` (and has `plain_text_body` of "Deploy finished"). What happens with `curl -d "Deploy finished"`?! STOP EVERYTHING! Gotta test what ActionText does with this. **I need to immediately test the `bin/rails runner` on these inputs:** * "Deploy finished" * "

module User::Role
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]
  end

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/user/bot.rb
module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  BOT_TOKEN_LENGTH = 32

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :created_bots, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id, dependent: :nullify

    before_validation :ensure_bot_password_digest, if: :bot?
    before_create :assign_bot_token, if: :bot?

    scope :without_bots, -> { where.not(role: :bot) }
    scope :bots_visible_to, ->(user) { user.administrator? ? active.bot : active.bot.where(creator: user) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def create_bot!(attributes = {})
      create! attributes.reverse_merge(creator: Current.user).merge(role: :bot)
    end

    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      return nil if bot_key.blank?

      bot = active.bot.find_by(bot_token: bot_key)
      bot if bot&.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(bot.bot_token, bot_key.to_s)
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    bot_token if bot?
  end

  def reset_bot_token
    update! bot_token: generate_bot_token if bot?
  end

  private
    def ensure_bot_password_digest
      self.password_digest = "" if password_digest.nil?
    end

messages.thinking:
**Controller Creation and Parameter Validation**

Okay, these routes are clean and well-defined, I like it: clearly mapping GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE to their corresponding actions. Now, I need to create the controllers: `bots_controller.rb` and `messages/by_bots_controller.rb`. And, I need to update the existing controllers, like `accounts_controller.rb`, `sessions_controller.rb`, etc., to exclude bots in certain contexts. Easy enough.

Wait a sec, before I jump into `Messages::ByBotsController`, I need to think through a potential vulnerability here. What happens with malformed JSON? If someone sends invalid JSON, like `curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "not json"`, I need to make sure the application doesn't blow up. Remember the difference between `request.path_parameters[:bot_key]` and `params[:bot_key]`!

Okay, here's the breakdown:
-   `request.path_parameters[:bot_key]` and `request.path_parameters[:room_id]` are *only* read from the URL path, never from the body, regardless of content type. No parsing happens.
-   `params[:attachment]` is *only* touched in a multipart request.
-   For non-multipart requests, I need to read `request.raw_post` directly.

Wait, how are parameters logged? Rails uses `request.filtered_parameters`, which includes `:bot_key`. If invalid JSON is sent, that still won't break anything. Wait... in Rails 8, the parsing happens lazily within `request.request_parameters`, which `process_action` might inspect, but as long as I use `request.path_parameters[:bot_key]`, it will be ok.

Okay, let's verify. `request.path_parameters[:bot_key]` is always populated for route params. And, path parameters are already percent-decoded.

Now, let's nail down this `Messages::ByBotsController` code:

-   `authenticate_bot`: Uses `User.authenticate_bot(request.path_parameters[:bot_key])`.
-   `set_room`: Uses `@bot.rooms.find_by(id: request.path_parameters[:room_id])`.
-   `create`: Reads `params[:attachment]` for multipart, otherwise reads `request.raw_post`.

WAIT!  I have to think about what happens if `params[:room_id]` isn't a valid numeric ID, like `"abc"` or `"not-a-room"`.

In SQLite, `@bot.rooms.find_by(id: "abc")` - what does that actually *do*?

OMG. I just realized something big. ActiveRecord casts strings to integers! SQLite will implicitly cast `"1abc"` to `1`, meaning it might find the wrong room. Oh wow! If I pass `"1abc"` to `Room.find_by(id:)` it will try to return room 1!

Okay, so if `room_id` is `"1abc"` or `"not-a-number"`:
-   `"not-a-number".to_i` is `0` -> returns `nil` -> 404. Good.
-   `"1abc".to_i` is `1` -> WOULD FIND ROOM 1.  Unless I add a check!

I need to add `return head :not_found unless room_id.to_s.match?(/\A\d+\z/)` to explicitly validate that `room_id` is a number and *only* then attempt to find the room. This makes me very happy.

Okay, now I can write all these controllers!

class Messages::ByBotsController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  skip_forgery_protection
  allow_unauthenticated_access

  before_action :authenticate_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def create
    if @message = create_message
      @message.broadcast_create
      head :created, location: message_path(@message)
    else
      head :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private
    def allow_browser(**)
      # Bot API accepts any HTTP client (curl, CI jobs, scripts) regardless of User-Agent.
    end

    def authenticate_bot
      if @bot = User.authenticate_bot(request.path_parameters[:bot_key])
        Current.user = @bot
      else
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      room_id = request.path_parameters[:room_id]
      @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: room_id) if room_id.to_s.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def create_message
      if multipart_request?
        create_attachment_message
      else
        create_text_message
      end
    end

    def create_attachment_message
      if attachment_param.present?
        @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(attachment: attachment_param, creator: @bot)
      end
    end

    def create_text_message
      if (body = read_raw_body).present?
        @room.messages.create!(body: body, creator: @bot)
      end
    end

    def attachment_param
      params[:attachment] if params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end

    def multipart_request?
      request.content_mime_type == Mime[:multipart_form]
    end

    def read_raw_body
      body = request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
      body = body.scrub unless body.valid_encoding?
      body if body.strip.present?
    end
end
EOF

class Users::SidebarsController < ApplicationController
  DIRECT_PLACEHOLDERS = 20

  def show
    all_memberships     = Current.user.memberships.visible.with_ordered_room
    @direct_memberships = extract_direct_memberships(all_memberships)
    @other_memberships  = all_memberships.without(@direct_memberships)

    @direct_placeholder_users = find_direct_placeholder_users
  end

  private
    def extract_direct_memberships(all_memberships)
      all_memberships.select { |m| m.room.direct? }.sort_by { |m| m.room.updated_at }.reverse
    end

    def find_direct_placeholder_users
      exclude_user_ids = user_ids_already_in_direct_rooms_with_current_user.including(Current.user.id)
      User.active.without_bots.where.not(id: exclude_user_ids).order(:created_at).limit([ DIRECT_PLACEHOLDERS - exclude_user_ids.count, 0 ].max)
    end

    def user_ids_already_in_direct_rooms_with_current_user
      Membership.where(room_id: Current.user.rooms.directs.pluck(:id)).pluck(:user_id).uniq
    end
end

**Analyzing Bot Message Handling and Avatar Uploads**

Okay, so I'm diving into how bot messages are handled, specifically focusing on the implications of accepting raw input and how that interacts with the underlying HTML rendering and sanitization. My initial thought was: "Zero assumptions about users!" meaning everything should render identically, but wait... a crucial question has popped up: what happens in cases where someone sends a `curl` request containing potentially tricky data or HTML entities via a real HTTP server like Puma?

Specifically, when a bot sends a message via `curl` with a `Content-Type` of `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, the raw body is directly interpreted. This means characters like `%`, `+`, `=`, `&`, and even UTF-8 emojis are passed as-is to the `Messages::ByBotsController`. Now, running this `curl` command: `curl -i -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" http://127.0.0.1:3000/rooms/1/<bot-code>/messages` the controller reads the raw post data, doesn't decode URL-encoded characters, and simply stores the complete raw body as the message content. This makes me ask: What happens when they include things like `d<e`? Remember earlier we checked the behavior for `"Deploy <v1.2.3> finished"` vs `"a < b && c > d"`! I need to ensure that the rendering of these bot messages, specifically around HTML elements, is safe.

I'm now re-examining the prompt.  It's clear that bots can post raw message bodies and that the application is expected to treat this input as the message content. The important thing is that the message is broadcast and triggers push notifications.

Here's the critical question: Do we save the raw body directly or should we escape it?

1.  **Pass raw body directly:** This would allow for formatted messages (bold, italic, links) but requires careful sanitization to prevent XSS.  If we pass raw HTML like `<script>alert(1)</script>` directly into the `Message` and rely on sanitization, the message's body is created with `<script>alert(1)</script>`, is rendered as empty and NO XSS happens.
2.  **HTML-escape:** This would make *every* HTML tag display literally as text.

I'm realizing Campfire itself is a good example.  `Messages::ByBotsController` specifically creates the message with the raw body, and then sanitization is applied.  Checking the code, `Message` models have `has_rich_text :body`, indicating they expect rich text.  Tests explicitly check for `SanitizeTags` and `SanitizeAttributes` to sanitize arbitrary HTML in the message body. In this case, `ContentFilters::SanitizeTags` only allows a safe subset of HTML tags (like `<a>`, `<b>`, `<i>`, etc.), and `SanitizeAttributes` strips dangerous attributes like `onclick` or `javascript:`.  So, passing the `body` directly is the Campfire standard.

Now I need to pivot to avatar uploads. How do invalid or large avatars get handled? I need to check how the `UsersController` and `Users::ProfilesController` handle these situations. It's time to check `app/models/user/avatar.rb`, `test/models/user/avatar_test.rb` and `test/controllers/users/avatars_controller_test.rb` to understand how avatars, including their validation and processing, are handled.

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot sets role, creator, empty password_digest, and unique bot_key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert_equal "", bot.password_digest
    assert_not_nil bot.bot_key
    assert bot.bot_key.length >= 24

    second_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Alert Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_key, second_bot.bot_key
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "creating a bot grants membership to all open rooms only" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
    assert_not_includes bot.rooms, rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "authenticate_bot authenticates active bots by bot_key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid-key")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key.swapcase)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key[0..-2])
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes its bot_token, removes non-direct memberships, and preserves messages" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    old_key = bot.bot_key
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(body: "Deploy complete", creator: bot)

    bot.deactivate
    bot.reload

    assert bot.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(old_key)
    assert_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", message.reload.creator.name
  end

  test "bots_visible_to scopes bots to creator for members and all active bots for admins" do
    kevin_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Kevin Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    jz_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "JZ Bot", creator: users(:jz))
    deactivated_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Old Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    deactivated_bot.deactivate

    assert_equal [ kevin_bot ], User.bots_visible_to(users(:kevin)).to_a
    assert_equal [ jz_bot ], User.bots_visible_to(users(:jz)).to_a
    assert_equal [ kevin_bot, jz_bot ].map(&:id).sort, User.bots_visible_to(users(:david)).pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "bot_token is filtered from inspect output" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Secret Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_not_includes bot.inspect, bot.bot_token
    assert_includes bot.inspect, 'bot_token: "[FILTERED]"'
  end

  test "destroying creator nullifies bot creator_id without error" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Orphan Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_nothing_raised { User.destroy_all }
    assert_not User.exists?(bot.id)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Messages::ByBotsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    @open_room = rooms(:hq)
    @closed_room = rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "posting a raw text message creates message, broadcasts to room and members, enqueues push, and returns 201 with Location" do
    body = "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅"

    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, +1 do
      assert_enqueued_with(job: Room::PushMessageJob) do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: body,
          headers: {
            "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
            "HTTP_USER_AGENT" => "curl/8.5.0"
          }
      end
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @open_room.messages.last
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert_equal body, message.plain_text_body

    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @open_room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @open_room, :messages ] do
      assert_select ".message__author strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /Deploy of v1\.2\.3 finished ✅/
    end
  end

  test "posting broadcasts unread room to members and not to non-members" do
    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
    outsiders = User.active.where.not(id: @closed_room.user_ids)
    assert outsiders.any?

    @closed_room.users.each do |member|
      assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(member.id), 1 do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: "Hello members #{member.id}",
          headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
      end
    end

    outsiders.each do |outsider|
      assert_no_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(outsider.id) do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: "Private update",
          headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
      end
    end
  end

  test "posting triggers web push notifications with bot name as author" do
    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(2)
      post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "Build green!",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
    end

    assert_response :created
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(2)
  end

  test "raw request body is preserved verbatim without form URL decoding or JSON envelope" do
    raw = "status=ok&percent=100%&expr=a+b=c"

    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: raw,
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal raw, @open_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting with application/json content type and non-JSON raw text still treats body as raw message" do
    raw = "plain text despite header"

    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: raw,
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/json" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal raw, @open_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting with an old browser user agent still succeeds" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "From old UA",
      headers: {
        "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain",
        "HTTP_USER_AGENT" => "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/114.0"
      }

    assert_response :created
  end

  test "posting an attachment creates an attachment message and returns 201 with Location" do
    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, +1 do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { attachment: fixture_file_upload("moon.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @open_room.messages.last
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert message.attachment?
    assert_equal "moon.jpg", message.plain_text_body
  end

  test "empty body and no attachment returns 422 Unprocessable Content" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "   \n\t  ",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { other: "value" },
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "multipart/form-data" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

  test "invalid bot code returns 401 Unauthorized" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, "wrong-bot-code"),
        params: "Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, "wrong.code.with.dots"),
        params: "Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized

    # Invalid bot code returns 401 even if room id is also bad
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(999_999, "wrong-bot-code"),
        params: "Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "deleted bot can no longer post messages and receives 401 Unauthorized" do
    old_key = @bot.bot_key
    @bot.deactivate

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, old_key),
        params: "Should fail",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "bad room id returns 404 Not Found" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(999_999, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :not_found

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url("not-a-room", @bot.bot_key),
        params: "Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :not_found

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url("#{@open_room.id}abc", @bot.bot_key),
        params: "Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "bot cannot post to a closed room until added and loses access when removed" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Knock knock",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    assert_response :not_found

    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Now inside!",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Now inside!", @closed_room.messages.last.plain_text_body

    @closed_room.memberships.revoke_from(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "After removal",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "bot joins newly created open rooms and can post there" do
    new_open_room = Rooms::Open.create_for({ name: "Announcements", creator: users(:david) }, users: users(:david))

    post room_bot_messages_url(new_open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Welcome!",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Welcome!", new_open_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "bot can post to a direct room it belongs to" do
    direct_room = Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(User.where(id: [ users(:kevin).id, @bot.id ]))

    post room_bot_messages_url(direct_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Direct ping!",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Direct ping!", direct_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "malicious HTML in bot message is sanitized in broadcast" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: '<script>alert(1)</script><a href="javascript:alert(2)" onclick="evil()">hi</a>',
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @open_room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @open_room, :messages ] do
      assert_select "script", count: 0
      assert_select "a[href^='javascript:']", count: 0
      assert_select "a[onclick]", count: 0
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /hi/
    end
  end

  private
    def wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(count)
      pool = Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.delivery_pool
      start = Time.now
      timeout = 0.5
      while pool.completed_task_count < count
        raise "Timeout waiting for pool tasks to complete" if Time.now - start > timeout
        sleep timeout / 10.0
      end
    end
end

Whoa, this is a fantastic find! Let me break down what I'm seeing. This trace is pointing directly at a crucial vulnerability in how Rails handles URL-encoded data, specifically in the context of `POST` requests. Looking at this backtrace, the error is originating from deep within Action Pack, specifically in `ActionDispatch::Request#POST` and, by extension, `ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters#parameters` and `ActionDispatch::Http::FilterParameters#filtered_parameters`. We are also getting this error within `ActionController::Instrumentation#process_action`.

The critical point here is the interaction with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. The application is attempting to decode the raw body using `URI.decode_www_form`, and this is where it's failing. The culprit? The presence of a `%` character in the data, such as in "100% complete." This triggers a `400 Bad Request` because the URL decoding interprets the `%` as the start of an encoded sequence, which is not valid in this context, causing the crash.

This is a real-world disaster in the making. Imagine a CI job, for instance, attempting to post a message with a percentage value—anything with a `%` symbol—and the entire deployment goes down with a 400 error! Think about `curl -d "Deploy 100% complete!"`, suddenly that is a problem and would have crashed. This bug would have been easily overlooked with a naive set of tests. Now, `test_posting_with_application_json` *might* have passed because the parsing logic may have been bypassed or handled differently if we are sending raw parameters.

The key to fixing this lies in understanding how the request parameters are being filtered and the point at which the decoding is attempted. We need to examine `ActionDispatch::Request#POST` and `ActionController::Metal#dispatch` more closely. The relevant files, `actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/request.rb` around line 414 and `actionpack/lib/action_controller/metal/instrumentation.rb` around line 66, should provide the answers.

Okay, this is great! I've been reviewing the code in `Messages::ByBotsController` and came across a potential improvement that could simplify things and make it more robust. Specifically, I'm focusing on the `dispatch` method and how it handles different `Content-Type` headers.

Currently, we check `request.content_mime_type == Mime[:multipart_form]`, but I'm concerned about potential errors if the `Content-Type` header is malformed. Digging into Rails 8.1, I discovered that `request.media_type` is actually a plain string (like `"multipart/form-data"` or `"application/x-www-form-urlencoded"` or `nil`) and, crucially, doesn't raise errors on malformed headers. This makes it a much safer and simpler option!

So, my plan is to refactor `dispatch` to use `request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"` instead. This cleaner approach also aligns with how we handle multipart requests elsewhere. Specifically, I will update `multipart_request?` to also use `request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"`.

Think about how this simplifies things! With this approach:
*   For a `curl` request with URL-encoded data, we set `request.request_parameters = {}`. Rack never tries to decode the payload, and `request.raw_post` gets the exact, untouched bytes.
*   For a `curl` request with an invalid `application/json` payload, we also set `request.request_parameters = {}`. Rails never tries to parse the JSON, and `request.raw_post` returns the raw data.
*   The same goes for plain text -  `request.request_parameters = {}` and we can directly get the contents of the payload.
*   Of course, for `multipart/form-data` uploads, `request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"` is true, Rack handles the multipart parsing correctly, and `params[:attachment]` becomes an `ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile`.
*   Also, if we receive a corrupted multipart body, Rack will handle the error. We can rely on Rack to raise `BadRequest` or return empty data in the event of an issue. This aligns with standard behavior for this media type.

Additionally, I'm looking at how we handle 404s in `BotsController#set_bot`, where we use `@bot = User.active.bot.find_by(id: params[:id])` and then `head :not_found unless @bot`. This approach provides clean 404 responses in both test and production. I'm going to ensure this 404 handling consistency throughout the codebase.

Let's refactor `Messages::ByBotsController` and `BotsController` to use this new approach and update the test files accordingly. Then, we can re-run the tests and verify that everything is working as expected. This refactor should streamline the code, improve its resilience to malformed requests, and maintain consistency in error handling across our controllers.

class Messages::ByBotsController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  skip_forgery_protection
  allow_unauthenticated_access

  before_action :authenticate_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def dispatch(name, request, response)
    request.request_parameters = {} unless request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    super
  end

  def create
    if @message = create_message
      @message.broadcast_create
      head :created, location: message_path(@message)
    else
      head :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private
    def allow_browser(**)
      # Bot API accepts any HTTP client (curl, CI jobs, scripts) regardless of User-Agent.
    end

    def authenticate_bot
      if @bot = User.authenticate_bot(request.path_parameters[:bot_key])
        Current.user = @bot
      else
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      room_id = request.path_parameters[:room_id]
      @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: room_id) if room_id.to_s.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def create_message
      if multipart_request?
        create_attachment_message
      else
        create_text_message
      end
    end

    def create_attachment_message
      if attachment_param.present?
        @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(attachment: attachment_param, creator: @bot)
      end
    end

    def create_text_message
      if (body = read_raw_body).present?
        @room.messages.create!(body: body, creator: @bot)
      end
    end

    def attachment_param
      params[:attachment] if params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end

    def multipart_request?
      request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    end

    def read_raw_body
      body = request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
      body = body.scrub unless body.valid_encoding?
      body if body.strip.present?
    end
end
EOF

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    no_store
    @bots = User.bots_visible_to(Current.user).ordered.with_attached_avatar
  end

  def new
    @bot = User.new(role: :bot)
  end

  def create
    @bot = User.new(bot_params.merge(role: :bot, creator: Current.user))

    if @bot.save
      redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    if @bot.update(bot_params)
      redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
    else
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate
    redirect_to bots_url, notice: "✓"
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = User.active.bot.find_by(id: params[:id])
      head :not_found unless @bot
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)
    end

    def bot_params
      params.require(:bot).permit(:name, :avatar).tap do |permitted|
        permitted.delete(:avatar) if permitted[:avatar].blank?
      end
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot sets role, creator, empty password_digest, and unique bot_key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert_equal "", bot.password_digest
    assert_not_nil bot.bot_key
    assert bot.bot_key.length >= 24

    second_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Alert Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_key, second_bot.bot_key
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "creating a bot grants membership to all open rooms only" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
    assert_not_includes bot.rooms, rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "authenticate_bot authenticates active bots by bot_key" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid-key")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key.swapcase)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key[0..-2])
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes its bot_token, removes non-direct memberships, and preserves messages" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    old_key = bot.bot_key
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(body: "Deploy complete", creator: bot)

    bot.deactivate
    bot.reload

    assert bot.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(old_key)
    assert_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", message.reload.creator.name
  end

  test "bots_visible_to scopes bots to creator for members and all active bots for admins" do
    kevin_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Kevin Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    jz_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "JZ Bot", creator: users(:jz))
    deactivated_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Old Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    deactivated_bot.deactivate

    assert_equal [ kevin_bot ], User.bots_visible_to(users(:kevin)).to_a
    assert_equal [ jz_bot ], User.bots_visible_to(users(:jz)).to_a
    assert_equal [ kevin_bot, jz_bot ].map(&:id).sort, User.bots_visible_to(users(:david)).pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "bot_token is filtered from inspect output" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Secret Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_not_includes bot.inspect, bot.bot_token
    assert_includes bot.inspect, "bot_token: [FILTERED]"
  end

  test "destroying creator nullifies bot creator_id without error" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Orphan Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_nothing_raised { User.destroy_all }
    assert_not User.exists?(bot.id)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Messages::ByBotsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    @open_room = rooms(:hq)
    @closed_room = rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "posting a raw text message creates message, broadcasts to room and members, enqueues push, and returns 201 with Location" do
    body = "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅"

    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, +1 do
      assert_enqueued_with(job: Room::PushMessageJob) do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: body.dup,
          headers: {
            "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
            "HTTP_USER_AGENT" => "curl/8.5.0"
          }
      end
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @open_room.messages.last
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert_equal body, message.plain_text_body

    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @open_room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @open_room, :messages ] do
      assert_select ".message__author strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /Deploy of v1\.2\.3 finished ✅/
    end
  end

  test "posting broadcasts unread room to members and not to non-members" do
    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
    outsiders = User.active.where.not(id: @closed_room.user_ids)
    assert outsiders.any?

    @closed_room.users.each do |member|
      assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(member.id), 1 do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: +"Hello members #{member.id}",
          headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
      end
    end

    outsiders.each do |outsider|
      assert_no_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(outsider.id) do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: +"Private update",
          headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
      end
    end
  end

  test "posting triggers web push notifications with bot name as author" do
    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(2)
      post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: +"Build green!",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
    end

    assert_response :created
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(2)
  end

  test "raw request body is preserved verbatim without form URL decoding or JSON envelope" do
    raw = "status=ok&percent=100%&expr=a+b=c"

    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: raw.dup,
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal raw, @open_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting with application/json content type and non-JSON raw text still treats body as raw message" do
    raw = "plain text despite header"

    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: raw.dup,
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/json" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal raw, @open_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting with an old browser user agent still succeeds" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +"From old UA",
      headers: {
        "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain",
        "HTTP_USER_AGENT" => "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/114.0"
      }

    assert_response :created
  end

  test "posting an attachment creates an attachment message and returns 201 with Location" do
    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, +1 do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { attachment: fixture_file_upload("moon.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @open_room.messages.last
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert message.attachment?
    assert_equal "moon.jpg", message.plain_text_body
  end

  test "empty body and no attachment returns 422 Unprocessable Content" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: +"",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: +"   \n\t  ",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { other: "value" },
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "multipart/form-data" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

  test "invalid bot code returns 401 Unauthorized" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, "wrong-bot-code"),
        params: +"Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, "wrong.code.with.dots"),
        params: +"Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized

    # Invalid bot code returns 401 even if room id is also bad
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(999_999, "wrong-bot-code"),
        params: +"Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "deleted bot can no longer post messages and receives 401 Unauthorized" do
    old_key = @bot.bot_key
    @bot.deactivate

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, old_key),
        params: +"Should fail",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "bad room id returns 404 Not Found" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(999_999, @bot.bot_key),
        params: +"Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :not_found

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url("not-a-room", @bot.bot_key),
        params: +"Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :not_found

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url("#{@open_room.id}abc", @bot.bot_key),
        params: +"Hello",
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "bot cannot post to a closed room until added and loses access when removed" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +"Knock knock",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    assert_response :not_found

    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +"Now inside!",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Now inside!", @closed_room.messages.last.plain_text_body

    @closed_room.memberships.revoke_from(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +"After removal",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "bot joins newly created open rooms and can post there" do
    new_open_room = Rooms::Open.create_for({ name: "Announcements", creator: users(:david) }, users: users(:david))

    post room_bot_messages_url(new_open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +"Welcome!",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Welcome!", new_open_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "bot can post to a direct room it belongs to" do
    direct_room = Rooms::Direct.create_for({ creator: users(:kevin) }, users: User.where(id: [ users(:kevin).id, @bot.id ]))

    post room_bot_messages_url(direct_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +"Direct ping!",
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Direct ping!", direct_room.messages.last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "malicious HTML in bot message is sanitized in broadcast" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: +'<script>alert(1)</script><a href="javascript:alert(2)" onclick="evil()">hi</a>',
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @open_room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @open_room, :messages ] do
      assert_select "script", count: 0
      assert_select "a[href^='javascript:']", count: 0
      assert_select "a[onclick]", count: 0
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /hi/
    end
  end

  private
    def wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(count)
      pool = Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.delivery_pool
      start = Time.now
      timeout = 0.5
      while pool.completed_task_count < count
        raise "Timeout waiting for pool tasks to complete" if Time.now - start > timeout
        sleep timeout / 10.0
      end
    end
end
EOF

Okay, so I was looking at `Rack::MethodOverride` and specifically `method_override_param`. I initially thought it was protecting against some obscure request issues but then, wait a minute, what about someone sending a `DELETE` request disguised as a `POST` with `_method=DELETE`? I remember that the `Rack::MethodOverride` rewinds `rack.input` and this is why `request.raw_post` still returns the exact raw body. I needed to ensure that no data could be accidentally exposed or improperly processed. I started wondering if `req.POST` could have cached some data in `env`, which could cause problems downstream, especially if combined with an empty `request.request_parameters`. I quickly wanted to test this with `curl` to make sure!

Specifically, I was concerned about a bot making a `POST` request with a sensitive `bot_key` and how it gets logged. The `filter_parameters` configuration should handle this, but I wanted to be extra sure the logging was correct, and that `filtered_parameters` covered everything. I was also concerned with the standard path logging in Rack/Rails. Rails' `filter_parameters` filters parameter hashes and `ActiveRecord#inspect` attributes, so I was fairly confident.

I then realized I needed to test the behavior of the API with various `curl` scenarios: `POST` with no `Content-Type`, `application/octet-stream`, `--data-binary` with multi-line text, and `-F "attachment=@..."` file uploads. I needed to confirm everything was handled correctly.

Representing bots as `User` records lets them participate in Campfire natively without special-casing rooms, memberships, messages, avatars, mentions, search indexing, Turbo Stream broadcasts, or web push notifications: - `users.bot_token` (nullable `string`, unique index) holds a 32-character cryptographically random alphanumeric token (`SecureRandom.alphanumeric(32)`), generated on creation for bots only. - `users.creator_id` (nullable `integer`, indexed FK to `users.id` with `on_delete: :nullify`) records which user created the bot. - `users.password_digest` is set to `""` for bots (cannot authenticate via password). - `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` automatically adds newly created bots to all `Rooms::Open`. `Rooms::Open` also grants membership to `User.active` (including bots) when new open rooms are created or closed rooms are opened. - `User.without_bots` excludes bots from human-only flows: account member lists/management (`/account/edit`, `/account/users`), password and transfer-link sign-in (`/session`, `/session/transfers`), bans (`/users/:id/ban`), and sidebar direct-message placeholders. ### Deletion / deactivation Deleting a bot (`DELETE /bots/:id`) calls `User#deactivate`, which: - sets `status: :deactivated` - clears `bot_token: nil` (immediately invalidating the credential) - deletes non-direct room memberships - preserves historical messages posted by the bot so chat transcripts remain intact. ### Authorization and credential hygiene - Any authenticated member can list their own bots, create bots, and edit/delete bots they created (`User::Role#can_administer?` checks `administrator? || self == record&.creator`). - Administrators see and can manage all active bots (`User.bots_visible_to`). - `BotsController#index` sets `Cache-Control: no-store` and `` and renders all bots on one page without pagination. - `User.authenticate_bot` validates `bot_key` against `User.active.bot` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. - `bot_token` and `bot_key` match `:token` and `:_key` in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, so both are filtered in logs and `ActiveRecord#inspect`. ### HTTP posting API `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`Messages::ByBotsController#create`): - Authenticates the bot first (`401 Unauthorized` on invalid/deleted bot code), then looks up the room scoped to `@bot.rooms` (`404 Not Found` for nonexistent, non-numeric, or non-member rooms). - Skips CSRF verification, cookie session auth, browser version gating, and form/JSON parameter parsing for non-multipart requests (so `curl -d "Build 100% done!"` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` is never rejected or decoded by Rack). - Accepts raw UTF-8 text body or a `multipart/form-data` upload in `attachment`; returns `422 Unprocessable Content` when both are absent/blank. - Creates the message with `creator: @bot`, broadcasts via `Message#broadcast_create` (which also triggers `Room#receive` unread updates and `Room::PushMessageJob` web push notifications), and responds `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`.
